findings.title: Commit subject omits ticket prefix
findings.problem: Commit 'teams-integ-1-foundation: add planning artifacts' uses a task-slug prefix instead of the required 'EPMCDME-14111: Description' format.
findings.impact: Breaks the documented ticket-traceable commit history convention this repo enforces, weakening traceability from commit to Jira ticket.
findings.recommendation: Reword the subject to 'EPMCDME-14111: add planning artifacts', or squash it into an adjacent EPMCDME-14111 commit before merge.

findings.title: MS Teams singleton lacks direct test
findings.problem: check_ms_teams_singleton is never exercised directly by any test; every test that reaches validate_ms_teams_request patches Settings.check_ms_teams_singleton itself instead of letting it run.
findings.impact: A typo in the query field name or an inverted setting_id comparison would silently break the per-project ms_teams singleton invariant in production without any test failing.
findings.recommendation: Add a direct unit test analogous to check_alias_unique's tests in tests/codemie/rest_api/models/test_settings_model.py, asserting the exact get_by_fields query shape and the existing/setting_id branch.

findings.title: MS Teams singleton race condition (TOCTOU)
findings.problem: Per-project ms_teams uniqueness is enforced only by check_ms_teams_singleton's read-then-write check; no DB-level unique constraint or index backs it in either alembic migration.
findings.impact: Two concurrent create requests for the same project can both pass the existence check before either insert completes, producing two ms_teams settings rows for the same project.
findings.recommendation: Add a partial unique index on settings(project_name) WHERE credential_type='MS_TEAMS' (or an equivalent DB constraint), and handle the resulting IntegrityError as a 409.

findings.title: Optional[str] used instead of str | None
findings.problem: check_ms_teams_singleton(cls, project_name, setting_id: Optional[str] = None) uses typing.Optional while the sibling new function validate_ms_teams_request correctly uses 'setting_id: str | None = None'.
findings.impact: Documented blocking Python style standard (code-quality.md) for new code is unmet.
findings.recommendation: Change the parameter to 'setting_id: str | None = None' to match the style already used in validate_ms_teams_request.

findings.title: MS Teams existence check leaks before permission
findings.problem: In both create_project_setting and update_project_setting, validate_ms_teams_request (which raises a 409 naming the project when an ms_teams integration already exists) runs before _check_permission / the Ability(user).can() ownership check.
findings.impact: A caller can probe for the existence of any project's ms_teams integration by supplying an arbitrary project_name, before the system has verified the caller has any access to that project.
findings.recommendation: Move the permission/ownership check ahead of the credential-type-specific validation block in both routers, so unauthorized callers never reach validate_ms_teams_request.

findings.title: project_name not validated in MS Teams request
findings.problem: validate_ms_teams_request never checks that request.project_name is non-empty before passing it to AssistantService.belongs_to_project and Settings.check_ms_teams_singleton; SettingRequest.project_name is Optional[str] = None at the API layer.
findings.impact: A request with project_name=None reaches belongs_to_project for every assistant id, which returns False for all of them, producing a confusing 'Invalid assistant_ids' 400 instead of a clear 'project_name is required' error.
findings.recommendation: Add 'if not request.project_name: raise ExtendedHTTPException(400, ...)' at the top of validate_ms_teams_request.

findings.title: assistant_ids elements not type-validated
findings.problem: assistant_ids_creds[0].value is only checked to be a non-empty list (CredentialValues.value: Any); individual elements are never validated to be strings before set(assistant_ids) (dedup check) or ', '.join(invalid_ids) (error message) run on them.
findings.impact: An unhashable element (e.g. a nested dict/list) crashes set(assistant_ids) with an unhandled TypeError, and a hashable non-string element (e.g. an int) that fails belongs_to_project crashes ', '.join(invalid_ids); both surface as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error.
findings.recommendation: Validate 'if not all(isinstance(a, str) for a in assistant_ids): raise ExtendedHTTPException(400, ...)' immediately after extracting assistant_ids, before the duplicate check.
